content:
olivia_customer: Hi team — our customer (ACME) just reported a regression in structured_output after the model swap to redwood/v4.1-weighted a few minutes ago. Their webhook consumer started throwing JSON parse errors.

aj_support: Uh oh. Do we have a sample payload?

olivia_customer: Pasting the request/response they sent (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/v4.1-weighted","mode":"structured_output","input":"Generate product JSON for an order"}'

Response body (truncated by their parser):

{"items":[{"id":"sku-123","qty":2,"price":19.99}],"total":39.98

// then some trailing text like: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 123

aj_support: Looks like the response is missing the closing brace or has extra streaming metadata appended. Did they use streaming?

olivia_customer: They say they used non-streaming. It fails intermittently (not every request). Works fine against redwood/v4.0-stable.

maria_ops: Deploy bot shows a canary config swap 3m ago where we changed kernel selection for v4.1 variants. deploy-bot: canary-deploy redwood/v4.1-weighted @region-us-west at 2008499800 by ci/cd

kevin_ml: Quick hypothesis — some quantized kernel is injecting a trailing newline plus an extra control chunk when tokenization hits EOS for certain prompts. That can corrupt strict JSON.

sam_engineer: I reproduced locally using the customer's prompt. Non-streaming call returned: 

```
{"items":[{"id":"sku-123","qty":2,"price":19.99}],"total":39.98}

<extra>
```

so there is an extra literal `<extra>` token appended. When I pin model to v4.0 it returns clean JSON.

aj_support: Can we capture the raw bytes at the serving runtime for a failing request? Need headers + body. Also what's the retry behavior — are they getting multiple partial chunks?

maria_ops: Added a temporary debug route that logs the final output for 5 failing requests. Please trigger a repro and paste the request ts here.

olivia_customer: Repro ids from the customer: req_12345, req_12347 (failed), req_12348 (succeeded). They said the failures line up with slightly higher latency (~180ms vs 120ms baseline) and occasionally a 502 -> client retries and concatenates streams.

kevin_ml: If retries are concatenating partial bodies we can end up with merged JSON fragments. Could be either a serving bug (not setting Content-Length properly on close) or a client-side concatenation issue.

sam_engineer: Quick check commands I ran: 

```bash
curl -s -D - -o /tmp/resp.bin \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/v4.1-weighted","mode":"structured_output","input":"Generate product JSON for an order"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
xxd /tmp/resp.bin | head
```

shows an extra 0x1E record separator followed by ascii "<extra>" on some runs. That record separator was introduced in the kernel output stream for a debug marker in the new runtime.

maria_ops: Oof. That matches the canary notes — we accidentally left a debug metadata separator enabled for some kernels. I'm rolling a hotfix to strip any non-JSON trailing markers for non-streaming responses. Patching now.

deploy-bot: rolling config patch to strip-runtime-markers from non-stream responses — rollout started at 2008500120 (canary 10%).

aj_support: For the customer: recommend pinning to redwood/v4.0-stable temporarily, and ask them to disable client-side concatenation or aggressive retry merging. I'll draft a support note.

olivia_customer: Got it — I'll tell the customer to pin and will update them that we have a hotfix in progress. Thanks.

kevin_ml: Follow-up action: add a regression test that verifies structured_output responses are valid JSON byte-for-byte under retries + partial reconnects. Also remove any debug separators from non-streaming code paths.

sam_engineer: Filed ENG-1247 for the regression test and ENG-1248 for kernel marker removal.

maria_ops: Hotfix rolled to 100% at 2008500300. Monitoring logs for 10m.

olivia_customer: Customer confirmed success after hotfix — no more parse errors for previously failing req ids. They kept the pin for 1 day and then unpinned and it was fine.

aj_support: Closing loop — I'm sending postmortem to the customer and adding an internal note. :white_check_mark:

olivia_customer: Thanks all.
